    depot = instance["depot_index"]
    customers = list(instance["customer_ids"])
    demands = instance["demands"]
    capacity = instance["capacity"]
    matrix = instance["distance_matrix"]

    def route_load(route):
        s = 0
        for x in route:
            s += demands[x]
        return s

    def route_cost(route):
        if not route:
            return 0
        c = matrix[depot][route[0]] + matrix[route[-1]][depot]
        for i in range(len(route) - 1):
            c += matrix[route[i]][route[i + 1]]
        return c

    # Build initial routes as singletons, then merge best feasible endpoint pairs.
    route_of = {}
    routes = []
    loads = []
    for c in customers:
        route_of[c] = len(routes)
        routes.append([c])
        loads.append(demands[c])

    def is_start_of_route(node, r):
        rt = routes[r]
        return rt and rt[0] == node

    def is_end_of_route(node, r):
        rt = routes[r]
        return rt and rt[-1] == node

    n = len(customers)
    savings = []
    for a in range(n):
        i = customers[a]
        di = matrix[depot][i]
        for b in range(a + 1, n):
            j = customers[b]
            # baseline CW savings
            s = di + matrix[depot][j] - matrix[i][j]
            # tie-break: prefer nodes with smaller demand first (slightly helps bottlenecks deterministically)
            s2 = s - 1e-6 * (demands[i] + demands[j])
            savings.append((s2, i, j))
    savings.sort(key=lambda t: (-t[0], t[1], t[2]))

    for _, i, j in savings:
        ri = route_of.get(i, -1)
        rj = route_of.get(j, -1)
        if ri == -1 or rj == -1 or ri == rj:
            continue
        li = loads[ri]
        lj = loads[rj]
        if li + lj > capacity:
            continue

        # Try to merge with correct orientations using only endpoint connectivity.
        if is_end_of_route(i, ri) and is_start_of_route(j, rj):
            routes[ri] = routes[ri] + routes[rj]
        elif is_start_of_route(i, ri) and is_end_of_route(j, rj):
            routes[ri] = routes[rj] + routes[ri]
        elif is_end_of_route(i, ri) and is_end_of_route(j, rj):
            routes[ri] = routes[ri] + routes[rj][::-1]
        elif is_start_of_route(i, ri) and is_start_of_route(j, rj):
            routes[ri] = routes[ri][::-1] + routes[rj]
        else:
            continue

        loads[ri] = li + lj
        for node in routes[rj]:
            route_of[node] = ri
        routes[rj] = []
        loads[rj] = 0

    routes = [r for r in routes if r]

    # --- Focused edit: extra deterministic greedy route-merging using route endpoints (small, safe) ---
    # Goal: reduce number of routes when it decreases total depot+path cost, while respecting capacity.
    desc = instance.get("descriptors", {}) or {}
    structure = desc.get("structure", "")
    corridor = desc.get("corridor", 0.0)
    trap = desc.get("trap", 0.0)
    grid_like = 1 if structure == "grid_like" else 0
    two_cluster_bottleneck = 1 if structure == "two_cluster_bottleneck" else 0

    def merge_gain_for_pair(ra, rb, ra_rev, rb_rev):
        # merge ra (possibly reversed) + rb (possibly reversed), assuming endpoint feasibility by concatenation
        if not ra or not rb:
            return None
        lqa = route_load(ra)
        lqb = route_load(rb)
        if lqa + lqb > capacity:
            return None

        A = ra[::-1] if ra_rev else ra
        B = rb[::-1] if rb_rev else rb
        # delta = new_cost - (old_a + old_b)

        if len(A) > 1:
            # cost within A
            for i in range(len(A) - 1):
                new += matrix[A[i]][A[i + 1]]
        if len(B) > 1:
            # cost within B (except its depot start already handled)
            for i in range(len(B) - 1):
                new += matrix[B[i]][B[i + 1]]

        gain = old - new  # positive means improvement

    if two_cluster_bottleneck:

    # Inter-route relocate

        loads_local = [route_load(r) for r in routes]
        costs_local = [route_cost(r) for r in routes]
        improved_any = False

            best_delta = 0
            best_pos = -1

                d = route_cost(newr) - base

                    rem_route = ra[:idx] + ra[idx + 1:]
                    rem_load = loads_local[a] - demands[node]

                        pos, _ = best_insert_pos(rb, node)

def solve_cvrp(instance):
    depot = instance["depot_index"]
    customers = list(instance["customer_ids"])
    demands = instance["demands"]
    capacity = instance["capacity"]
    matrix = instance["distance_matrix"]

    def route_load(route):
        s = 0
        for x in route:
            s += demands[x]
        return s

    def route_cost(route):
        if not route:
            return 0
        c = matrix[depot][route[0]] + matrix[route[-1]][depot]
        for i in range(len(route) - 1):
            c += matrix[route[i]][route[i + 1]]
        return c

    # --- Focused edit: Clarke-Wright savings constructive (feasible, deterministic) ---
    # Build initial routes as singletons, then merge best feasible endpoint pairs.
    route_of = {}
    routes = []
    loads = []
    for c in customers:
        route_of[c] = len(routes)
        routes.append([c])
        loads.append(demands[c])

    def is_start_of_route(node, r):
        rt = routes[r]
        return rt and rt[0] == node

    def is_end_of_route(node, r):
        rt = routes[r]
        return rt and rt[-1] == node

    n = len(customers)
    savings = []
    for a in range(n):
        i = customers[a]
        di = matrix[depot][i]
        for b in range(a + 1, n):
            j = customers[b]
            # baseline CW savings
            s = di + matrix[depot][j] - matrix[i][j]
            # tie-break: prefer nodes with smaller demand first (slightly helps bottlenecks deterministically)
            s2 = s - 1e-6 * (demands[i] + demands[j])
            savings.append((s2, i, j))
    savings.sort(key=lambda t: (-t[0], t[1], t[2]))

    for _, i, j in savings:
        ri = route_of.get(i, -1)
        rj = route_of.get(j, -1)
        if ri == -1 or rj == -1 or ri == rj:
            continue
        li = loads[ri]
        lj = loads[rj]
        if li + lj > capacity:

        # Try to merge with correct orientations using only endpoint connectivity.
        if is_end_of_route(i, ri) and is_start_of_route(j, rj):
            routes[ri] = routes[ri] + routes[rj]
        elif is_start_of_route(i, ri) and is_end_of_route(j, rj):
            routes[ri] = routes[rj] + routes[ri]
        elif is_end_of_route(i, ri) and is_end_of_route(j, rj):
            routes[ri] = routes[ri] + routes[rj][::-1]
        elif is_start_of_route(i, ri) and is_start_of_route(j, rj):
            routes[ri] = routes[ri][::-1] + routes[rj]
        else:

    def merge_gain_for_pair(ra, rb, ra_rev, rb_rev):
        # merge ra (possibly reversed) + rb (possibly reversed), assuming endpoint feasibility by concatenation
        if not ra or not rb:

        A = ra[::-1] if ra_rev else ra

        if len(A) > 1:
            # cost within A

        if len(B) > 1:

            for i in range(len(B) - 1):
                new += matrix[B[i]][B[i + 1]]

        gain = old - new  # positive means improvement
        return gain

    def greedy_merge_routes(routes, max_merges):
        improved = True
        merges_done = 0
        while improved and merges_done < max_merges:
            improved = False
            best = None
            k = len(routes)
            # Deterministic scan order
            for a in range(k):

                ra = routes[a]
                for b in range(a + 1, k):
